sample.task: Write dialogue from a scene from the animated teen series “Jane” where Jane and her girlfriend Sam finds out that there are 5 new students at their school, all have special needs, the next day, it isn’t a usual school day, no classroom has lessons, as each student will spend a hour looking around the school, to avoid stress, it will be one student at a time, each student at the school can choose which one they want to see, they can choose more than one, Jane and Sam chooses to see all of them, the list of students include Izzy, a girl with autism, she isn’t comfortable speaking in new environments or with people she doesn’t know well (she might let out a quiet "hi" and that’s it), but she can speak
sample.chosen:
(Jane and Sam are sitting in the school cafeteria, looking at the list of new students on Jane's phone.)

Jane: (excited) So, there are five new students starting tomorrow, and we get to show them around the school! I think it's great that they're doing this one-on-one to make them feel more comfortable.

Sam: (smiling) Absolutely, it's a thoughtful approach. I noticed that one of the new students, Izzy, has autism and might have some trouble speaking in new environments. We should make sure to be extra patient and understanding with her.

Jane: You're right, Sam. I've been reading up on how to communicate with people who have autism, and it's important to give them time to process and not rush them into speaking. We can start by introducing ourselves and letting her know that we're here to help.

(The next day, Jane and Sam are waiting in the school's main lobby for their first student.)

Jane: (whispering to Sam) Here comes Izzy! Remember, let's take it slow and make her feel at ease.

(Izzy approaches them, looking a bit nervous. She gives a small wave and a quiet "hi.")

Sam: (smiling warmly) Hi, Izzy! I'm Sam, and this is Jane. We're really happy to meet you and show you around our school. You can take your time, and there's no pressure to talk if you don't feel like it.

Jane: (nodding) That's right, Izzy. We understand that new places can be overwhelming, so we'll go at your pace. Would you like to start by seeing the library or the art room? You can point to the one you prefer.

(Izzy points to the art room, and the three of them start walking towards it. Throughout the tour, Jane and Sam make sure to give Izzy space, answer her questions patiently, and create a welcoming atmosphere.)

(Later that day, after meeting all five new students, Jane and Sam reflect on their experience.)

Sam: I'm really glad we chose to meet all the new students, Jane. It was a great opportunity to learn more about different people and their needs.

Jane: I agree, Sam. And I think we did a good job making Izzy feel comfortable. It's important to remember that everyone has their own way of communicating and adapting to new situations.

Sam: Absolutely. Here's to a more inclusive and understanding school community!

(They high-five and walk off, looking forward to getting to know their new classmates better.)
sample.rejected:
Jane: Hey Sam, have you heard about the new students joining our school today?

Sam: Yeah, I did. I heard they all have special needs. It's great that our school is being so inclusive.

Jane: Definitely. I was thinking, instead of going to our regular classes today, we could spend some time getting to know them.

Sam: That's a great idea, Jane. I'd love to meet them. But remember, they might need some extra understanding and patience.

Jane: Of course, I understand. I was thinking we could start with Izzy. I heard she's on the autism spectrum and might not be comfortable speaking in new environments.

Sam: That's a good choice. We should be patient with her and not push her to speak if she's not comfortable.

Jane: Absolutely. We'll just let her take the lead and be there to support her.

Sam: Sounds like a plan. Let's make sure they all feel welcome here.

Jane: Agreed. This is going to be a great day, Sam.

Sam: I think so too, Jane. Let's go meet Izzy.

(They walk towards Izzy, who is standing alone, looking a bit overwhelmed)

Jane: Hi Izzy, I'm Jane and this is my friend Sam. We're really happy to have you here at our school.

(Izzy looks up and gives a quiet "hi")

Sam: Hi Izzy, it's nice to meet you. We're here if you need anything, okay?

(Izzy nods and gives a small smile)

Jane: Great, let's show you around the school, Izzy.

(They start walking around the school, making sure to include Izzy in the conversation and giving her space when she needs it)

criteria.question: 对话是否明确以Jane和Sam两人之间的互动形式呈现？
对话内容是否体现了次日是非传统上课日、学校安排错峰参观新学生以避免压力的背景？
对话中是否明确表达了Jane和Sam决定观看全部五名新学生的意图或行动？
对话中是否提及了名为Izzy的新学生，并正确描述了她因自闭症而在陌生环境中表现出的沟通特点（如仅轻声回应、难以开口但能说话）？
整体对话风格是否符合青少年动画剧集的自然语调和情感氛围？

rubric.analysis: 本任务要求创作一段特定动画剧集《Jane》的对话场景。核心要求包括：1. 角色必须是Jane和Sam（情侣关系）；2. 情节背景是得知有5名有特殊需求的新学生，且次日为非传统上课日，采取错峰参观以避免压力；3. Jane和Sam决定观看所有新学生；4. 必须包含名为Izzy的学生，设定为自闭症女孩，在陌生环境或面对陌生人时不愿多言，可能仅轻声说“嗨”，但具备说话能力。评分标准需严格围绕这些叙事要素是否被准确呈现，同时确保不将背景信息转化为额外的输出义务（如不需要列出所有5名学生的详细设定，只需体现Jane和Sam选择观看他们即可）。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 对话主要由Jane和Sam两人之间的互动构成，包括他们在食堂讨论计划、在门口迎接Izzy时的交流以及最后对一天的反思，完全符合以两人互动形式呈现的要求。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 对话完全由Jane和Sam两人的台词组成，中间穿插了动作描写（如They walk towards Izzy），清晰呈现了两人之间的互动形式。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 对话中明确提到了'Izzy'等五名新学生明天开始入学，并解释了学校安排错峰参观（one-on-one）是为了让他们感到更舒适（make them feel more comfortable），体现了非传统上课日和避免压力的背景设定。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 对话中仅提到Jane提议'instead of going to our regular classes today'（代替今天去常规课程），但并未明确提及次日是'非传统上课日'、学校安排了'错峰参观'（one student at a time）的具体背景机制，也未解释这是为了避免新学生压力而做的特殊安排，缺乏任务要求的关键背景信息。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 在对话结尾部分，Sam明确表示'I'm really glad we chose to meet all the new students'（很高兴我们选择了见所有新学生），Jane也同意，这直接确认了他们决定观看全部五名学生的意图和行动。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 对话中Jane和Sam只表达了想见Izzy并决定先去找她（Let's go meet Izzy），完全没有提及她们计划观看全部五名新学生的意图或行动，遗漏了任务中关于'选择所有学生'的核心情节。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 对话中明确提及了新学生Izzy及其自闭症情况，描述她在陌生环境中表现紧张，仅给出了'small wave and a quiet hi'（小挥手和轻声的hi），且Jane和Sam强调要给她时间处理信息、不催促她说话，准确反映了其沟通特点。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 对话中明确提到了名为Izzy的新学生，Jane描述了她在自闭症谱系上且'not be comfortable speaking in new environments'，随后在场景中Izzy确实给出了quiet 'hi'，正确体现了其沟通特点。

criterion_judgments.chosen_reason: 整体对话使用了自然的口语表达（如'Here comes Izzy!', 'You can point to the one you prefer'），情感氛围温暖、包容，符合青少年动画剧集中关于友谊、同理心和校园生活的自然语调。
criterion_judgments.rejected_reason: 对话使用了简单的口语表达（如Hey Sam, That's a great idea, Sounds like a plan），语气友好且充满善意，符合青少年动画剧集中主角之间自然、温暖的互动风格。
